The Japanese (驚く) and Vietnamese (ngạc nhiên) expressions primarily correspond to the intransitive sense ('to feel/be surprised'). However, the provided English definition/sense context ('astonishment, amazement, surprise') strongly indicates that the intended core learning sense is the state of being surprised, making the alignment exact across all three languages for this core meaning.
